kurz: Mustard seeds only turn hot once they are crushed and mixed with water. An enzyme then creates the heat, and vinegar sets how hot it stays.
bild_im_kopf: Like a camera: water opens the shutter, vinegar closes it. Whatever happens in between stays in the picture.
sicherheit: Sharp fumes rise when grinding: do not lean right over the blender.
ergebnis: About one small jar of mustard.
haltbarkeit: Several months in the fridge. Vinegar and salt preserve it.
material: 75 g mustard seeds (yellow for mild, brown for hot)
2–3 tbsp white wine or cider vinegar
½ tsp salt, 1–2 tbsp sugar or honey
verwendung: With sausages, in vinaigrette, in mayonnaise as a helper for the emulsion.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Soak the seeds in water for a few hours
schluesselmomente.warum: They swell and are easier to crush. Cold water makes the mustard hotter, warm water milder.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Drain and grind coarsely or finely with salt and sugar
schluesselmomente.warum: When crushed, an [[enzym|enzyme]] in the seeds meets its partner substance. Together they form the hot mustard oils.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Wait a few minutes, then stir in vinegar
schluesselmomente.warum: Acid stops the enzyme. Vinegar early gives mild mustard, vinegar later gives hot.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Fill into a jar and let it mellow in the fridge for 2–3 days
schluesselmomente.warum: Fresh, it is biting and bitter. Over time it turns rounder and milder.
